4. Counterbalance forklifts form the primary transport fleet for receiving, put-away support, replenishment supply and dispatch staging.
5. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts.
6. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.
7. Operate counterbalance trucks within rated capacity at all times and observe load centres, attachment limits and battery-care instructions posted in the charging area.
8. Reach trucks serve the high bays for put-away and retrieval at height.
9. The fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays.
10. Reach trucks are rated at 2.0 t.
11. Assign reach work only to operators trained for high-bay operation and report mast, camera or guidance faults for entry in the repair log without delay.
12. Electric pallet jacks handle horizontal movement of prepared pallets in receiving, picking support and outbound staging.
13. The fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks.
14. Retain electric jacks for dock work, replenishment feeding and wrapped-pallet positioning where pedestrian separation can be maintained.
15. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks.
16. Deploy hand pallet jacks for short moves, workstation supply and backup during charging or maintenance downtime.
17. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers.
18. Route every outbound pallet through wrapping before staging and confirm film containment at base, corners and top layer before release to the dock.
19. The site has 1 cardboard baler.
20. Feed only clean cardboard to the baler, follow the lock-off and chamber-clearing instructions, and stack finished bales in the designated collection area for removal.
21. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.
22. Inspect the leveller, dock seal and restraint before positioning handling equipment at the door and report hydraulic leaks, deformed decks or missing controls for repair logging.
23. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners.
24. Draw scanners at shift start, confirm battery level and scan function, and return faulty units to the charging station for replacement. Store charged units only in the designated chargers.
25. Coordinate fleet availability across shifts to protect receiving, replenishment, picking and dispatch flow, and notify supervision immediately when unserviceable equipment reduces planned throughput.

title: Authorisation and daily checks
text:
1. Operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks only if you are a designated forklift operator acting under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

2. Seek authorisation as a new forklift operator only from the warehouse manager. Do not accept verbal clearance from any other role as authority to drive.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. That accountability includes the decision who may drive materials handling equipment. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators, and no operator may start unsupervised driving without that recorded authorisation.

3. Present your licence, training certificate and site induction record for verification before authorisation.

4. Complete familiarisation on the assigned truck type and work area before first use. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks, so confirm which equipment classes your authorisation covers.

5. Perform the documented daily pre-use check on every forklift before first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. The daily forklift check happens before first use each day, without exception for late arrivals, truck swaps or short tasks.

6. Walk around the truck and check forks, carriage, chains, hoses, mast operation, steering, brakes, parking brake, lights, beacon, horn, reversing alarm, mirrors, seat belt, seat adjustment, tyres and wheels, battery charge and connections, hydraulic oil level and visible leaks.

7. Test all controls from the operator seat at standstill, including lift, lower, tilt, side-shift where fitted, inching, travel in both directions and emergency stop function.

8. Record the check on the daily sheet for that truck, with date, truck identity, hour reading, defects found and your signature. Do not use a truck with an open defect entry from a previous check.

9. Tag out and report any defective truck immediately and remove its key to the designated control point. Do not attempt repair, adjustment or bypass of safety devices.

10. Hand over the completed daily sheet to the incoming operator at shift change and brief any faults, changed handling behaviour or battery state. A truck changing hands during the day does not require a second full documented check unless it has been tagged, repaired or involved in an incident, but each new operator must read the current daily record before driving.

11. File all daily sheets for audit under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and retain defects for follow-up action. The warehouse manager reviews authorisations and outstanding truck defects as part of site safety sign-off.

title: Safe operation rules
text:
1. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Fasten the belt before selecting direction and keep it fastened until the truck is fully parked with the brake applied. Never override, bridge or remove the belt interlock.

2. Complete the documented daily check before first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Withdraw any truck with defective brakes, steering, horn, lights, seat belt, forks, chains or tyres from service immediately. Report the defect for repair and take a serviceable truck instead.

3. Observe the indoor limit inside the building.

Drive forklifts at no more than 8 km/h in all indoor aisles, storage areas and handling zones. Adjust further down for congestion, floor conditions, visibility and load stability.

4. Limit speed in the outdoor yard to the posted yard maximum.

Drive at no more than 12 km/h in the outdoor yard, including trailer manoeuvring areas and routes to the dock approaches. Increase following distances on wet, icy or uneven surfaces.

5. Reduce speed to 5 km/h in every marked pedestrian zone and at every marked pedestrian crossing.

Anticipate pedestrians at aisle ends, doorways, staging areas and crossings even where markings are worn. Sound the horn at blind corners and stop where sight lines are blocked.

6. Approach every dock ramp and leveller approach at crawling speed.

Drive at no more than 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches, square to the leveller and without sharp steering on the slope. Confirm the leveller, dock seal and restraint are correctly set before driving on or off the trailer bed.

7. Maintain full control of the load on all routes.

Travel with forks low, mast tilted back and load against the backrest, looking in the direction of travel. Reverse where the load blocks forward vision, use a banksman where local rules require it, and never carry passengers or lift persons unless the equipment is specifically approved for that task.

8. Give way to pedestrians everywhere and stop rather than edge past.

Keep clear of the segregated walkways, halt at crossings, and wait until pedestrians have cleared the manoeuvring envelope before proceeding. Lower the forks, neutralise controls and apply the parking brake before stepping off, even for brief stops.

9. Park only in designated areas without obstructing aisles, doors, emergency routes or charging points.

Remove the key, apply the parking brake and lower the forks fully to the floor on shutdown. Report every contact, tip, slip or near miss on the shift so the truck can be rechecked before return to work.

title: Evacuation and drills
text:
1. Execute PR-14 Emergency evacuation exactly as written whenever the alarm sounds, a supervisor orders evacuation, or danger threatens the building.
2. Stop all work immediately on hearing the alarm. Shut down handling equipment in a safe position where time permits and leave loads stable in the aisle.
3. Leave the building by the nearest safe escape route. Walk briskly to the designated assembly point and keep walkways and dock approaches clear for emergency response.
4. Assist visitors and contractors in your immediate area to the nearest exit. Direct them to follow marked escape routes to the assembly point.
5. Close fire doors behind you where you pass through them. Do not stop to collect personal belongings, complete system entries, or move pallets.
6. Report to the assembly point without delay and remain there until released. Assemble by shift and work area so the roll call proceeds quickly and accurately.
7. Complete roll call at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. No employee, contractor, or driver may return inside until the roll call confirms all persons present.
8. Place the on-duty shift supervisor in charge of the evacuation. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and therefore controls movement, accounts for staff, and liaises with emergency services on site.
9. Instruct the shift supervisor to coordinate search information, missing-person reports, and access control during the incident. Keep all other staff at the assembly point and prevent re-entry until the all-clear is given.
10. Prohibit re-entry for any reason before the authorised release. Reopen the building only after the roll call is complete and the responsible authority confirms the site safe for return.
11. Conduct an evacuation drill every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Treat each drill as a real evacuation and require full clearance of the building to the assembly point.
12. Vary drill timing across shifts so all floor staff practise evacuation, assembly, and roll call. Record attendance, evacuation time, and observations for each drill.
13. Require the shift supervisor to review every incident report arising from a real evacuation or drill. Identify blocked routes, failed doors, missing lists, or poor discipline and assign corrective actions.
14. Debrief each shift immediately after the drill. Explain faults found, repeat correct routes and assembly discipline, and confirm understanding before resuming normal work.
15. Keep escape routes, emergency exits, and assembly access free at all times. Report blocked exits, damaged signage, or faulty alarms for immediate repair and note them in the handover where relevant.

title: Safety inspections and incidents
text:
1. Inspect all pallet racking under a documented safety inspection every month.
Schedule the inspection to cover every aisle in rotation so no bay remains unchecked beyond the monthly interval.
Record beam damage, upright deformation, missing pins, anchor condition and load notices in the inspection log.

2. Verify during each inspection that each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg.
Compare the displayed bay load against the system weight for the stored pallets.
Mark any overloaded bay out of service immediately until the load is corrected.

3. Assign the physical inspection and follow-up repairs to the maintenance technician.
The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
Ensure every defect, adjustment and component replacement appears in the repair log with date and signature.

4. Isolate damaged uprights, bent beams or leaking pallets on discovery.
Unload the affected levels with suitable handling equipment before any repair attempt.
Release the bay back to operation only after the repair log confirms its release.

5. Photograph structural damage before moving stock or starting repairs.
Attach the photographs to the inspection record for traceability.
Retain the records for audit alongside the monthly inspection sheets.

6. Submit an incident report for every near miss, injury, collision, dropped pallet, rack strike or spill.
Complete the report before the end of the shift in which the event occurred.
Include location, equipment involved, persons present and immediate actions taken.

7. Forward every incident report to the on-duty supervisor without delay.
The shift supervisor reviews every incident report.
Do not close the report until the review, root cause and corrective actions are documented.

8. Apply immediate containment after any incident involving racking.
Cordon off the affected bay and adjacent working area with barriers.
Notify downstream operations to reroute put-away, replenishment and picking tasks.

9. Investigate rack impacts jointly with operations and maintenance.
Examine floor markings, handling routes and load condition for contributing factors.
Define retraining, layout changes or additional protection where the findings require it.

10. Track all open inspection findings and incident actions to closure.
Review overdue items at the daily operational meeting until each is signed off.
Escalate any repeat overload, repeat impact or overdue structural repair for management decision.

11. Hand over outstanding defects and open incidents between shifts in writing.
State the bay numbers concerned, the isolation measures in place and the next planned step.
Confirm that the incoming responsible person has understood the restrictions before resuming work nearby.

title: Cold-chain and hazmat controls
text:
1. Execute PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all chilled stock movements, storage and temperature checks without exception.
2. Maintain Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C for all temperature-controlled inventory.
3. Verify the Zone E temperature manually each shift with the calibrated display and site thermometer.
4. Record each shift reading immediately in the temperature log with time and initials.
5. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
6. Keep the cold zone at or below +6 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
7. Close Zone E doors promptly after every entry and exit to protect the +2 to +6 °C range.
8. Isolate any pallet showing temperature abuse and escalate it under PR-12 Cold-chain handling before further movement.
9. Prohibit staging chilled pallets outside Zone E except for immediate loading or put-away under active control.
10. Execute PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all classified hazardous goods, storage checks and spill actions.
11. Store all hazmat only inside the fenced hazmat cage inside Zone F, never in general racking or open floor areas.
12. Limit total holdings in the hazmat cage to no more than 3,000 kg at one time across all SKUs and containers.
13. Plan cage occupancy on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets.
14. Check cage stock weight before every put-away and reject any receipt that would exceed 3,000 kg.
15. Keep incompatible classes segregated within the cage according to label instructions and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Inspect containers, bunds, labels and extinguishers each shift and clear any obstruction from cage access and spill kits.
17. Contain drips immediately, ventilate the area, don the specified protective equipment and notify supervision under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
18. Forbid ignition sources, food and unauthorised entry inside the cage and ensure spill residues leave only through the approved waste route.

title: End-of-shift handover
text:
1. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change of shift without exception. Treat the handover as a formal transfer of responsibility for the floor, the loads and all open issues.

2. Plan the handover around the fixed shift pattern. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Start preparation in sufficient time that the incoming shift can take control promptly at the changeover hour.

3. Assign ownership of the handover to the outgoing shift supervisor. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The outgoing shift supervisor remains accountable until the incoming shift supervisor has accepted the floor in person.

4. Assemble the handover information before meeting the incoming shift. Collect the status of inbound work in progress, put-away backlogs, picking progress against open tasks, packed containers awaiting release, staged outbound loads awaiting collection, and any resources taken out of service.

5. Walk the floor status point by point with the incoming shift supervisor. State clearly which work areas are clear, which tasks are partly complete, which equipment is unavailable, and where staff are currently deployed. Do not leave any active exception, delay or customer commitment unmentioned.

6. Hand over all open safety and quality matters explicitly. Report any incident under review, any damaged stock awaiting transfer, any quarantined goods awaiting decision, any spill cleaned or awaiting re-inspection, and any area requiring extra supervision during the next shift. Confirm that the incoming shift supervisor understands the required follow-up actions.

7. Record the handover in the shift log. Enter the date, the handover time, the names of the outgoing and incoming supervisors, the operational status of each work area, the list of incomplete loads and tasks, and the list of open safety, damage and service issues carried forward. Require both supervisors to sign the entry to confirm transfer.

8. Brief the incoming floor staff immediately after the supervisor-to-supervisor exchange. Communicate priorities for the first hours, changes to task assignments, known shortages or delays, and any special instructions for handling sensitive loads. Direct any questions to the incoming shift supervisor before work resumes.

9. Close the outgoing shift in an orderly manner. Secure documentation, return shared devices to their designated point, leave workstations and handling equipment in a safe condition, and confirm that no task is left in an unsafe or uncontrolled state. Release the outgoing team only when the incoming shift supervisor confirms readiness to assume control.

title: Speed limits and shared areas
text:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation on every truck movement inside the building and in the outdoor yard.
2. Inside the building forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h at any time, including all zones and connecting aisles.
3. In the outdoor yard forklifts must not exceed 12 km/h, adjusting further for weather, surface conditions and visibility.
4. Within marked pedestrian zones and crossings forklifts must slow to 5 km/h and give way to pedestrians on foot.
5. On dock ramps and leveller approaches forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h, approaching squarely and without sharp turning.
6. Under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse pedestrians retain priority in all shared areas and at every crossing point.
7. Inside Zone A, the receiving zone with inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection, keep to designated truck routes and stop for banksmen where directed.
8. Throughout Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, travel only along the centre of the rack storage aisles, which are 3.0 m wide.
9. Across Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, reduce speed in advance, sound the horn at blind corners and never overtake a pedestrian.
10. In Zone D, the dispatch zone with outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, stage and manoeuvre only in marked areas and maintain clearance from staged pallets and loading equipment.
11. Use the main transport aisles, which are 4.0 m wide, for longer travel and for passing; do not use rack storage aisles as through routes.
12. Keep the segregated pedestrian walkways, which are 1.2 m wide, completely clear of pallets, cages and handling equipment at all times.
13. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks and remain responsible for safe speed, lookout and separation from pedestrians on every trip.
14. Fasten the seat belt before moving off, since forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and stop the truck to adjust the load or controls.
15. Report speeding, near misses and blocked walkways or crossings immediately, noting that the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
16. Stop work and secure the truck if visibility, congestion or pedestrian presence prevents maintaining the applicable limit and priority rules safely.

title: Walkways, aisles and dock areas
text:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse in all shared traffic areas. Keep forklift and pedestrian movements separated wherever marked routes exist.

2. Use only marked segregated pedestrian walkways for walking through the warehouse. Those walkways are 1.2 m wide and are separated from truck routes by markings and barriers where installed.

3. Do not step outside walkways or designated crossings to take shortcuts across aisles. Wait behind the marked line at crossings until the forklift operator has acknowledged you and stopped.

4. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor. No person may enter floor, aisle or dock areas without a high-visibility vest and safety footwear class S3.

5. Drive centrally in main transport aisles and expect two-way truck traffic. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and must be kept clear of pallets, waste and staged goods at all times.

6. Control speed strictly by location. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.

7. Reduce speed to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to every pedestrian and stop completely where sight lines are restricted.

8. Enter rack storage aisles with caution and reduced speed. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; do not overtake, do not park, and sound the horn before entering blind aisle ends.

9. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving in Zone A, covering unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch in Zone D, covering outbound staging in front of the doors.

10. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; check the leveller is correctly seated before driving on or off the trailer.

11. Observe dock discipline at Zone A and Zone D. Do not approach an open door, enter a trailer, or start loading or unloading until authorised. Keep dock staging clear of walkways and crossings.

12. Follow all instructions from dispatchers at the docks. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.

13. Direct visiting drivers to the designated waiting location and keep them clear of manoeuvring trucks. Do not allow drivers to walk the floor unescorted or to enter Zone A or Zone D without high-visibility vests and safety footwear class S3.

14. Report blocked walkways, damaged barriers, faded markings, faulty dock levellers or unsafe staging to supervision immediately. Do not resume normal traffic through the affected area until it has been cleared and released.

title: Driver authorisation and truck checks
text:
1. Operate material-handling equipment only under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and only if you are an authorised operator. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

2. Obtain authorisation before driving any powered truck. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

3. Remember that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Do not permit unauthorised driving, passengers, or use of a truck reported as faulty.

4. Know the fleet you are assigned to. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.

5. Select the correct truck for high-bay work. The fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays. Reach trucks are rated at 2.0 t.

6. Use pedestrian equipment only within its design purpose. The fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks.

7. Respect the rated capacity on every lift. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Never exceed the data-plate capacity of the truck in use.

8. Complete the documented pre-use check each day before starting work. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. The daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.

9. Record brakes, steering, tyres and wheels, forks and mast, chains, horn, lights, beacon, reverse alarm, mirrors, seat belt and guarding, battery charge and leaks, hydraulic oil level and leaks, and emergency stop where fitted. Remove a defective truck from service immediately, tag it clearly, and hand the checklist to supervision.

10. Report every fault for repair without delay. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Do not restart a truck taken out of service until it has been cleared.

11. Fasten the seat belt before moving off. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Keep body parts inside the cage, apply the parking brake when leaving the seat, and lower the forks when parked.

12. Drive at a speed that always allows safe stopping. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

13. Keep to a safe pace outside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.

14. Slow early for people and level changes. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

15. Park only in designated areas, switch off, and secure the key. Leave keys only through the authorised handover arrangement and never lend an authorised truck to an unauthorised person.

title: Required PPE and seat belts
text:
1. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor without exception for role, task or duration of visit.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Keep the vest fastened and visible over outer clothing during receiving, storage, picking, dispatch and transit through shared areas. Replace soiled, torn or faded vests before starting work.

2. Wear safety footwear class S3 whenever present on the warehouse floor, including offices access routes crossing operational areas.

Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Ensure footwear is laced, intact and suitable for wet dock leveller approaches and outdoor yard crossings. Report damaged footwear to supervision and withdraw from floor duties until replaced.

3. Fasten the seat belt before moving any forklift and keep it fastened whenever the truck is moving.

Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Apply the rule to counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and other ride-on equipment covered by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Stop the truck safely if the belt loosens, slips or jams, then readjust before continuing.

4. Operate only equipment assigned under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and follow pedestrian controls under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. Conduct pedestrian interaction strictly under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, giving way at marked crossings and maintaining separation from segregated walkways. Never carry passengers, bypass restraints or defeat interlocks.

5. Enforce PPE and seat-belt compliance continuously throughout the shift.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Challenge any person without hi-vis or S3 footwear immediately and stop any moving truck whose operator is unrestrained. Record refusals or repeated non-compliance as incidents for review.

6. Maintain site-wide accountability for operations, safety and final sign-offs, including PPE standards.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Authorise exemptions only through documented risk assessment where justified, never verbally on the floor. Withdraw authorisation for unsafe practices until corrective action is complete.

7. Store spare vests and replacement footwear accessibly outside the floor so compliance causes no delay.

Issue compliant sizes before shift start to visitors, contractors and temporary staff. Prohibit entry to the floor until hi-vis and S3 requirements are met in full.

8. Check seat-belt condition during the daily truck check required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Reject any truck with a cut, frayed, jammed or missing belt and tag it out of service. Log the defect for maintenance and use only a released replacement truck.

9. Brief every shift on pedestrian visibility and restraint discipline as part of normal supervision.

Demonstrate correct vest wearing, S3 use and belt adjustment during induction and toolbox talks. Correct shortcuts on the spot and confirm understanding before allowing work to resume.

10. Treat PPE and seat-belt failures as safety incidents, not minor deviations.

Escalate injuries, near misses and wilful breaches through incident reporting without delay. Use findings to reinforce PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse across all shifts.

title: Racking and stacking limits
text:
1. Respect the rated limits of all storage structures in Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Never place more weight or height on racking or floor stacks than this instruction allows, and never climb on racking to reach stock.

2. Limit each rack bay to at most 2,700 kg total load. Calculate the bay total from the gross weight of every pallet level within that bay before putting away the next pallet. Distribute heavy pallets to lower levels where the rack design requires it, and leave any bay showing deflection, cracking or impact damage unloaded until cleared.

3. Keep every pallet within its gross weight allowance. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check the system weight or weigh indication before put-away and before replenishment. Reject overweight, unstable or overhanging pallets for rework and do not place them into high-bay positions.

4. Stack free block-stacked pallets only to the permitted height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Apply both limits together, so the lower of the two controls the stack. Build stacks square, interlocked and on sound pallets, with heavier units at the base.

5. Maintain clear operating clearances around racking at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Do not stage pallets, waste, chargers or handling equipment inside these aisles. Keep pallet overhang, stretch film tails and loose strapping outside the aisle profile.

6. Operate handling equipment in racking strictly under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Approach bays squarely, lift and lower smoothly, and confirm adequate headroom before raising a load to height. Stop work immediately if the truck contacts uprights, beams or bracing, barrier off the affected bay, and report the impact without delay.

7. Support the monthly integrity regime for racking. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Report bent uprights, missing safety pins, damaged beams, loose floor fixings and leaking goods to supervision on the same shift, and do not reload a quarantined bay.

8. Treat any suspect stack as unsafe until examined. Re-stack leaning columns, re-wrap loose loads, and transfer damaged pallets to quarantine under escort. Never pull a pallet from the bottom of a block stack, never stand pallets on edge against racking, and never leave a raised load unattended in the aisle.

title: Supervision and shift handover
text:
1. Accountability for site safety rests with the warehouse manager at all times. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

2. During staffed hours that accountability is exercised through direct floor supervision. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

3. Staffed operation is organised in two shifts. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.

4. Cover continues without interruption into the afternoon and evening. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

5. Remain under the control of the on-duty shift supervisor throughout your shift. Follow instructions on task allocation, traffic control, use of equipment and response to abnormal conditions.

6. Inform the shift supervisor immediately of any injury, near miss, damage to racking or equipment, spill, fire alarm or unsafe behaviour. Do not leave the scene unsafe while awaiting assistance.

7. Complete the required report for every safety event before leaving the site. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report.

8. Maintain continuity of safety information across shift changes. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change between Shift 1 and Shift 2.

9. Include in the handover all open safety matters from the outgoing shift. Hand over outstanding incident reports, injuries under follow-up, damaged racking or equipment taken out of use, spill clean-up in progress, pedestrian or traffic restrictions in force, and any area left under special control.

10. Check with the incoming shift supervisor that the handover has been understood before starting new work. Do not assume that guards, barriers, spill kits, fire exits or traffic controls are in normal condition after a shift change.

11. Walk your assigned area at the start of the shift. Confirm that walkways are clear, racking appears undamaged, emergency routes are accessible and required guards are in place, then report defects to the shift supervisor.

12. Never work on the floor without an appointed shift supervisor present. Outside Shift 1 and Shift 2 hours the building is not in normal supervised operation, so do not enter operational zones unless expressly authorised under supervised arrangements.

13. Support the warehouse manager in closing the safety loop. Provide complete information for final sign-offs, cooperate with investigations directed by the shift supervisor, and apply corrective actions instructed after review.

title: Cold zone rules
text:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every pallet, carton and tote stored in Zone E.

Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Treat any deviation from that band as a cold-chain failure, not as a local fluctuation. Never store ambient, frozen or uncontrolled goods in Zone E to save space or time.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times.

Monitor door openings, defrost cycles and loading dwell times because each one drives temperature downward or disrupts airflow. Keep the doors closed except for active put-away, replenishment or loading, and report icing, pooling water or uneven cooling without delay.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +6 °C at all times.

During warm weather, frequent access or equipment heat can push the upper limit quickly. Limit personnel entry to assigned tasks, switch off idle handling equipment inside the chamber, and escalate any upward trend before the limit is reached.

4. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift.

Use the calibrated display and the manual check defined in PR-12 Cold-chain handling, then record the reading, time and your name in the designated log. Across shift changes, communicate the last verified reading and any door or plant faults as part of handover.

5. Wear mandatory protection before entering Zone E.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including all work inside the cold zone. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, including wet or cold floors in Zone E. Add suitable thermal layers and gloves for prolonged chilled work, keeping cuffs, laces and hems clear of pallets and rollers.

6. Control movements and behaviour inside the chilled area.

Walk at a steady pace on potentially slippery surfaces, use handrails where provided, and never run to warm up. Handle chilled cartons with dry hands or appropriate gloves, stack them stably, and clean up condensation or spillages immediately to prevent slips.

7. Protect product integrity during every transfer.

Plan picks and put-aways so chilled goods remain inside Zone E until the moment of movement. Stage outbound chilled pallets only for immediate loading and return inbound chilled pallets to Zone E without intermediate storage in ambient areas.

8. Escalate alarms, suspect stock and equipment faults immediately.

Notify the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, of any temperature alarm, door failure, refrigeration fault, or pallet that feels warm, thawed or damp. Isolate suspect stock as directed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and prevent its picking, packing or dispatch until cleared.

9. Keep accountability for cold-chain safety unambiguous.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including calibration, maintenance priorities and final decisions on temperature-abused stock. The shift supervisor controls chilled work on the shift, enforces PR-12 Cold-chain handling, confirms each manual verification, and ensures only fit staff work extended periods in low temperatures.

title: Hazmat storage rules
text:
1. Confine all classified hazardous goods to the fenced hazmat cage inside Zone F. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Undertake no hazmat storage elsewhere on site.

2. Recognise the physical limits of the cage. Inside Zone F the hazmat cage covers 60 m2. Plan all receipts, put-away and picking around that footprint. Keep access routes, operating clearance and emergency access free at all times.

3. Observe the maximum stock for the cage without exception. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Hazmat cage stock weight must be checked before every put-away and any receipt exceeding 3000 kg rejected.

4. Convert the weight limit into pallet spaces during planning. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. On that basis the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Treat lighter pallets by their actual recorded weight rather than by count alone.

5. Wear the required personal protection for every entry and every handling task around the cage. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Add any task-specific protection required by the product label and safety data sheet.

6. Execute all storage, movement and documentation under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Inspect containers for leaks, damage and correct labelling before put-away. Secure incompatible products apart using the provided segregation provisions. Keep labels facing outward for identification during checks.

7. Maintain strict order inside the 60 m2 enclosure. Place only sealed, labelled and stable units in their designated positions. Stack nothing against fencing, doors or safety equipment. Remove empty pallets, waste packaging and unused equipment without delay. Report damaged containers, missing labels or faulty fittings for immediate action under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.

8. Accept accountability at site level. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate overstock risk, unauthorised access, repeated labelling failures or any doubt about classification before continuing work. Leave the cage in a safe, closed and clearly signed condition after each activity.

title: Spills, quarantine and damage
text:
1. Contain every spill immediately under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Stop the source if safe to do so, cordon the affected floor area, prevent liquid reaching drains and aisles, and alert surrounding staff without leaving the hazard unattended.

2. During any spill response wear high-visibility vests as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Keep safety footwear class S3 mandatory on the warehouse floor laced and intact, and add task-specific protection required by PR-13 before handling spilled containers, absorbents or contaminated packaging.

3. Notify the shift supervisor at once for any injury, near miss, spill, damaged racking or unsafe behaviour. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, takes control of the scene, decides on isolation, ventilation or evacuation of the immediate area, and coordinates clean-up and disposal.

4. Record every spill and contamination event in an incident report before the end of the shift. Describe substance, quantity, location, persons exposed, containment actions and photographs where taken, and submit the report for review without delay.

5. Ensure the shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Check that containment was complete, that waste was segregated correctly, that affected stock was identified, and that corrective actions for cleaning, retraining or equipment repair are assigned and closed.

6. Transfer all damaged, leaking, suspect-temperature or contaminated units to quarantine in Zone F without exception. Handle damaged goods thereafter only under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, keeping quarantine stock physically separated, clearly labelled and excluded from saleable inventory until formally released.

7. Remember that Zone F holds the value-added services area. Carry out inspection, sorting, repacking assessment, photography and valuation only inside the quarantine area in Zone F, maintaining clear access for inspection and preventing mixing with conforming VAS work.

8. Photograph damage before repacking or sorting, preserve labels and batch data, and value each damaged-goods proposal at cost price. Segregate intact inner units from destroyed packaging, retain samples where required, and prepare the written recommendation for restock, rework or scrap.

9. Obtain write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any damaged stock. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR, recorded with quantity, value, reason and supporting photographs.

10. Escalate larger losses to the warehouse manager without splitting consignments to avoid the threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR only on documented evidence and completed quarantine inspection.

11. Release quarantine holdings only after inspection, approval and system clearance. Return conforming stock to its assigned location, route rework through re-inspection, dispose of scrap through the approved waste stream, and file approvals with incident and stock records for audit.

title: Reporting incidents
text:
1. Report every injury, near miss, collision, dropped pallet, rack strike, spill, fire alarm activation and equipment fault without delay.
2. Notify the shift supervisor immediately from the scene by radio, telephone or in person and secure the area against further movement.
3. Remember the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and remains your first point of contact for any unsafe condition.
4. Complete the incident report form before leaving the shift, giving time, exact location, persons involved, equipment involved, witnesses and a factual description of what happened.
5. Forward each completed report to the shift supervisor for review on the same shift, as the shift supervisor reviews every incident report.
6. Preserve evidence until released by supervision: do not move damaged racking, spilt product, broken pallets or vehicles except to prevent immediate danger.
7. Transfer damaged stock to the quarantine area in Zone F and identify each pallet or carton with date, location found, incident reference and reporter name.
8. Handle all damage valuation, photography and disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and do not scrap, rework or restock affected units without written approval.
9. Obtain approval for every damaged-goods write-off before posting any adjustment in the system.
10. Submit write-offs up to 750 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval and retain the signed valuation with the incident file.
11. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
12. Attach the approval, photographs, scanner records and quarantine transfer note to the incident report for audit.
13. Include all open incidents, injuries, damage transfers to quarantine and pending write-off approvals in PR-15 End-of-shift handover to the incoming shift supervisor.
14. Monitor corrective actions assigned at handover until closed and report any recurrence, failed containment or missing approval to supervision immediately.

title: Evacuation and assembly point
text:
1. Activate PR-14 Emergency evacuation immediately on fire alarm, confirmed smoke or fire, gas suspicion, major spill, structural failure, or on direct instruction from the shift supervisor.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and therefore takes command of every evacuation on that shift until relieved. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and assumes overall control when present.

2. Stop all handling work at once across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.

Lower forklift forks to the floor, apply the parking brake, switch off the truck, and leave keys secured where local instruction requires. Leave pallets, scanners and pallet jacks where they stand if moving them would delay exit.

3. Leave the building by the nearest safe pedestrian exit.

Do not use lifts if fitted, do not run, and do not return for personal belongings, paperwork or equipment. Keep pedestrian walkways and main aisles clear for movement and assist visitors, drivers and contractors to the exits.

4. Keep all 8 dock doors and dock approaches clear for emergency access.

Do not move a trailer, open a dock leveller, or stage goods in doorways during the alarm. Forklift operators already in the yard must park clear of access roads and proceed on foot to the assembly point.

5. Proceed directly to the designated assembly point and remain there.

Walk in small groups, stay clear of the building facade and roadway, and do not gather at dock aprons or car park entrances. Account for colleagues who were working in enclosed areas such as the cold zone, hazmat cage, quarantine area and value-added services area.

6. Report to the shift supervisor for roll call without delay.

Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, so use the daily attendance record, visitor book and driver log to reconcile everyone expected on site. Call out names loudly, confirm absentees last seen location, and pass that information to emergency services on arrival.

7. Obey the roll call, then re-entry order without exception.

Roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building. Do not re-enter to search for missing persons, retrieve goods, restart equipment or check stock unless directed by emergency services under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

8. Release the building only through the person in charge.

The shift supervisor confirms the all-clear with emergency services, authorises controlled re-entry, and briefs returning staff on restricted areas. The warehouse manager reviews the outcome, signs off corrective actions, and ensures follow-up on safety and operational impacts.

9. Rehearse this routine every quarter.

An evacuation drill runs every quarter and tests alarm audibility across receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch, cold, value-added and office areas, exit discipline, assembly-point control and roll-call accuracy on both shifts. Treat each drill as a live evacuation and record attendance, timings and lessons learned.

title: Inspections, drills and follow-up
text:
1. Complete the documented pre-use check on every forklift each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation before first use each day.
2. Record brake function, steering response, horn, lights, forks, mast chains, tyres, fluid leaks, battery charge and overhead guard condition on the daily checklist and sign with truck identity, date and operator name.
3. Remove any truck with a failed check from service immediately, attach a prohibition tag at the steering wheel and notify the shift supervisor for reassignment of work.
4. Instruct replacement drivers to perform their own documented pre-use check each day even where the truck was already checked earlier on the same shift roster.
5. Maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment through the maintenance technician, including forklifts, reach trucks, pallet jacks, rack frames, beams, levellers, seals and restraints.
6. Log all repairs in the maintenance record with equipment identity, fault description, parts fitted, date completed and release signature before returning equipment to operation.
7. Examine all high-bay racking through a documented safety inspection every month, checking uprights, beams, bracing, fixings, load notices, bay markings and out-of-service tags.
8. Bar further loading of any damaged or overloaded bay until unload, repair and repair-log release are confirmed and the out-of-service marking is formally lifted.
9. Verify cold-zone temperature by manual check each shift, using the calibrated display and independent thermometer reading to confirm continued compliance with chilled storage requirements.
10. Document each manual verification with time, measured value, checker name and corrective action where deviation is found, filing the entry in the cold-zone log before shift handover.
11. Escalate any temperature deviation under PR-12 Cold-chain handling without moving affected pallets except for controlled isolation and assessment.
12. Assemble for evacuation practice under PR-14 Emergency evacuation every quarter, treating the drill as a full operational evacuation with alarms, wardens, routes and assembly point control.
13. Call roll at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building during both drills and real evacuations, accounting for staff, visitors, contractors and drivers by name or badge number.
14. Prohibit re-entry until the on-duty shift supervisor confirms the building is safe and releases personnel row by row from the assembly point.
15. Practice specific drill scenarios in rotation, including blocked exits, cold-zone evacuation in protective clothing, hazmat-cage spill with exclusion zone and dock-area evacuation with trailers in place.
16. Debrief every drill immediately at the assembly point, noting evacuation time, missing persons, communication gaps, blocked routes and equipment faults for the drill record.
17. Review every incident report through the shift supervisor, linking inspection findings, drill observations and injury or near-miss reports to preventive actions with owners and deadlines.
18. Monitor completion of follow-up actions at the next shift handover and weekly safety review, escalating overdue repairs, retraining or procedural changes until closed.
19. Close each incident only after corrective action is verified on the floor, documentation is complete and affected staff have been briefed on changed practice.
20. Retain daily forklift checklists, monthly racking inspection reports, shift temperature logs, quarterly drill records and incident review notes for audit and trend analysis.
21. Brief incoming shifts on any open equipment restrictions, racking exclusions, temperature alerts or pending drill actions during the supervisor-to-supervisor exchange before briefing floor staff.
22. Confirm understanding by requiring questions from operators, pickers, inbound staff and dispatchers before resuming full operations after any inspection failure, alarm or drill.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. Accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, the warehouse manager holds ultimate authority for Harbourwick 3PL Ltd. performance against plan, compliance and customer commitments.
2. Directing both staffed periods, Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, the warehouse manager sets resourcing, priorities and escalation cover across the week.
3. Approving all overtime personally, only the warehouse manager may approve overtime, including extensions required to complete inbound, outbound or stocktaking work.
4. Signing stocktake results exclusively, only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
5. Commissioning the annual wall-to-wall count, a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year under the warehouse manager's direction, with daily cycle counts continuing under stock control supervision.
6. Authorising every new forklift operator individually, only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
7. Governing damaged-goods write-offs above threshold, damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
8. Reserving higher-value decisions to this post, the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR, while the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
9. Supervising quarantine valuation and system posting discipline, the warehouse manager verifies that approvals precede adjustments and that write-off evidence is complete before sign-off.
10. Delegating returns disposition to shift leadership, the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns, with the warehouse manager auditing compliance and customer outcomes.
11. Entrusting dock scheduling to despatch control, the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, with the warehouse manager intervening only on conflicts, capacity risk or service failure.
12. Requiring prompt incident review on shift, the shift supervisor reviews every incident report, with the warehouse manager owning follow-up actions, trend review and closure.
13. Owning readiness for PR-14 Emergency evacuation, the warehouse manager ensures drills, assembly control and liaison arrangements remain effective through the shift supervisors.
14. Sponsoring disciplined PR-15 End-of-shift handover, the warehouse manager holds supervisors to full information transfer and confirmed acceptance at every change of shift.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. Run one assigned shift in full charge of floor staff and incident response.
2. Direct Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, according to roster.
3. Report to the warehouse manager, who remains accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
4. Allocate inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns staff, maintenance support and dispatch activity for the shift.
5. Supervise Zone A, the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
6. Supervise Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
7. Supervise Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
8. Supervise Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
9. Supervise Zone E, the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
10. Supervise Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
11. Enforce mandatory high-visibility vests for everyone on the warehouse floor.
12. Enforce mandatory safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor.
13. Review every incident report arising on the shift and direct immediate containment, first response and escalation.
14. Lead evacuation under PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
15. Control the quarterly evacuation drill on shift, account for all personnel at the assembly point and ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
16. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
17. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval before any system posting.
18. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling, confirming restock, rework or scrap.
19. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change of shift and remain accountable until the incoming shift supervisor has accepted the floor in person.
20. Brief the incoming supervisor on labour, equipment status, overdue orders, cold-zone integrity, quarantine holdings, incidents and open safety actions.

During the shift the supervisor stays visible on the floor, prioritises safety over throughput and stops any unsafe operation. Absences, equipment faults and zone congestion are rebalanced across Zones A to F without delaying outbound commitments. All decisions, approvals and incident reviews are recorded in the shift log for traceability.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads across all staffed shifts.
2. As scheduling owner, the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and maintains the daily transport plan without gaps or double bookings.
3. Within Zone D, the dispatch zone, outbound staging in front of docks 5-8 remains under dispatcher control from pallet staging through loading to departure.
4. Coordination with Zone A covers the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, ensuring inbound arrivals do not conflict with outbound movements.
5. Across the building the dispatcher manages all 8 dock doors as a single resource, with dock doors 1-4 serving inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serving outbound dispatch.
6. Under PR-01 Inbound receiving, dispatchers sequence arrivals so the document check happens BEFORE unloading, and no vehicle is called to doors 1-4 without complete booking documentation.
7. Under PR-06 Outbound dispatch, dispatchers authorise each load release only when wrapping, labelling, quantity reconciliation and transport documents are complete.
8. Capacity planning uses fixed outbound throughput: there are 4 outbound dock doors and each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.
9. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for planning carry a payload of 26000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions for load building.
10. For full-weight planning, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
11. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, and the dispatcher rejects any load plan exceeding trailer payload or floor positions.
12. Local deliveries allocated to the van respect its limits: our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg with 6 pallet positions, and takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
13. Total outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, derived from doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer, and dispatchers cap bookings at that ceiling.
14. Throughout the shift dispatchers work beside the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, escalating labour shortfalls, door faults and trailer rejections without delay.
15. Final accountability for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs rests with the warehouse manager, and dispatchers obtain required approvals for overtime, over-capacity bookings or exceptional movements.
16. At shift change dispatchers contribute load status, door allocation and carrier ETAs to PR-15 End-of-shift handover and remain available until the incoming team accepts control.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving from document check to system booking.

Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Operators report for their assigned shift, either Shift 1 which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

2. Before any trailer is opened, verify the booking, delivery note and purchase order quantity against the scheduled load.

At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading. Do not start unloading where documents are missing, quantities disagree or damage is visible from outside until the exception has been escalated under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

3. During unloading, count every carton and pallet, check outer packaging condition, labels and expiry dates where applicable, and segregate quantity variances and visible damage.

Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system. Record inspection results in the WMS and on the delivery paperwork without delay.

4. Operate pallet handling equipment within the receiving area to move inbound pallets to inspection and booking lanes, keeping pedestrian routes and dock approaches clear at all times.

Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Sign out a scanner at shift start, confirm each booking scan, and return the unit for charging at shift end.

5. Book inspected goods into the system immediately after inspection, print or activate pallet labels, and confirm weight and dimensions.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Reject overweight or unstable pallets for rework before booking.

6. Stage booked pallets by destination for release to PR-02 Put-away to storage.

Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Direct general pallets for Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Direct chilled pallets for Zone E, which is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Direct value-added, quarantine and returns-related receipts for Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

7. Hand over staged stock to forklift operators for put-away only after system booking is complete, ensuring each pallet carries its identifier and destination.

Never release unbooked goods to storage aisles or dispatch areas.

8. Wear prescribed personal protective equipment throughout all receiving work.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

9. Work under the direction of the shift team structure at all times.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow tasking, report variances, damage and missing documents immediately, and request reassignment before leaving Zone A. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. The role covers pallet movements between receiving, storage, picking, dispatch and value-added areas under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

1. Operate only after authorisation. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. No operator starts unsupervised truck work without that authorisation recorded.
2. Complete the documented pre-use check each day. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day, and the daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.
3. Operate the assigned fleet within rated capacity. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.
4. Observe site speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.
5. Slow for people and ramps. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
6. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Give way on segregated pedestrian walkways which are 1.2 m wide, keep clear of walkway markings, and use the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles for travel and the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles only at controlled speed.
7. Wear mandatory personal protection on the floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
8. Execute put-away and replenishment moves to instruction. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for transfers from Zone A to Zone B, and PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces for transfers from bulk storage to Zone C.
9. Serve all operating zones as tasked. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Zone F holds the value-added services area.
10. Respect storage limits in Zone B. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high.
11. Handle hazardous loads only under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, which holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Check hazmat cage stock weight before every put-away and reject any receipt exceeding 3000 kg.
12. Report to shift control. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate defects, damage and unsafe conditions immediately and stop the affected truck or operation until cleared.

title: Pickers
text:
1. Execute customer order picking in Zone C against scanner tasks under PR-04 Order picking, working only from the active task queue on the assigned handheld WMS scanner.
2. Attend Zone C at shift start, understanding that Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
3. Confirm pick-face availability before commencing work, since pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces.
4. Collect replenished stock transferred from bulk storage without diverting reserve pallets, noting that Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
5. Recognise the scale of reserve storage, where the high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions.
6. Follow the directed pick sequence location by location, scanning each location and unit as prompted and never advancing the task manually.
7. Ensure picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.
8. Transfer verified order containers to the designated handover point for PR-05 Packing and labelling without delay or interim storage.
9. Move completed pallets and containers toward Zone D when instructed, where Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
10. Observe the pallet limit at all times, as a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
11. Operate assigned handling aids safely within pedestrian and equipment areas, drawing from the fleet of 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.
12. Share the pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners responsibly with inbound staff, logging on at shift start and logging off at shift end.
13. Report scanner faults, damaged labels, empty locations, and quantity variances to the floor lead immediately and remain at the location until reassigned.
14. Wear mandatory personal protection throughout the warehouse floor, because high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
15. Work the rostered pattern as directed, where Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
16. Report to the on-duty leadership chain on every shift, where the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
17. Acknowledge site accountability, in that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2. Packing staff execute PR-05 Packing and labelling for every order container before release toward dispatch.
3. Within the shift structure, the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
4. For site accountability, the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
5. Zone F holds the value-added services area.
6. Returns are inspected in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling.
7. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision.
8. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery.
9. Check delivery documentation, authorisation and reason for return at receipt, then move units to the inspection point without mixing uninspected and inspected stock.
10. Scan-verify returned units against the return record, assess condition and quantity, and segregate proposed restock from proposed rework and proposed scrap.
11. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns.
12. Forward approved restock only through system booking to its designated storage location.
13. Route approved rework to the designated rework flow and route approved scrap and damaged units under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
14. The quarantine area is in Zone F.
15. Transfer damaged units found during returns inspection to quarantine and hold them pending valuation and write-off approval.
16. Every scrap and damaged-goods proposal is valued before seeking approval, with the approval path set by value.
17. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
18. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, granted by the warehouse manager.
19. Operate packing benches to the order specification: verify items by scan, select the specified carton or container, pack, seal and apply the correct labels.
20. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners.
21. Use the handheld WMS scanner for all returns, packing and labelling transactions and return faulty units to the charging point.
22. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers.
23. Wrap outbound pallets to base-to-top stability before staging for collection.
24. The site has 1 cardboard baler.
25. Break down empty cartons, bale cardboard and clear strapping and waste from work areas during the shift.
26. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
27. Stage packed, labelled and wrapped containers and pallets for transfer to Zone D without blocking walkways or dock approaches.
28. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
29. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
30. Report quantity variances, damage, missing documents, scanner faults and any unsafe condition to the shift supervisor immediately.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. Own inventory accuracy across all storage locations through cycle counts, recounts and adjustments in line with PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
2. Under the rotating zone schedule, execute cycle counts every working day covering Zone B, Zone C, Zone E and Zone F, using the shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners.
3. Within Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, control all 2,400 pallet positions and confirm each pallet including its load weighs at most 900 kg.
4. Across Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, verify pick-face quantities, correct put-away of replenishment and timely clearance of variances.
5. Throughout Zone E, the cold zone providing chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C, manually verify temperature each shift and record any stay below +2 °C or above +6 °C for escalation.
6. Inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, monitor stock held in the quarantine area in Zone F and inside the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
7. For the hazmat cage inside Zone F covering 60 m2, enforce the limit of no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat at one time, equivalent to at most 3 full-weight pallets. Check hazmat cage stock weight before every put-away and reject any receipt exceeding 3000 kg.
8. Before any stock adjustment is posted, arrange a second count of the location, as a second count happens before adjustment under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
9. After recount and investigation, prepare adjustments for approval, noting only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results and the warehouse manager remains accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
10. Coordinate the full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year, including move freezes, count teams, recounts, sign-off and posting, alongside the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
11. Enforce storage discipline during every count: each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, and free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height or 3 pallets high.
12. Support PR-09 Damaged-goods handling by valuing affected stock and routing write-offs above 750 EUR for warehouse-manager approval.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Each employee reports to the shift supervisor running the shift, while the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2. On each shift the technician coordinates directly with the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, for fault reports, isolations and release back to service.
3. Across the building, which has 8 dock doors, responsibility covers all fixed dock equipment, with each of the 8 dock doors having a dock leveller plus its seal, restraint and controls.
4. Within Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, the technician safeguards the high-bay racking that provides 2,400 pallet positions, where each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
5. Under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, the mobile fleet under care comprises 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.
6. Beyond trucks, Dispatch equipment supported includes 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and 1 cardboard baler, including film carriages, electrics and scheduled cleaning.
7. Before first use each day, the daily forklift check is verified as complete, since every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day and no truck may enter service with an open safety defect.
8. Throughout working hours, high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, without exception in plant rooms or dock pits.
9. During any test drive or relocation after repair, forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and the technician shall ground any truck with a defective restraint.
10. Every month racking gets a documented safety inspection, recording beam deflection, upright damage, missing pins, anchor condition and load-sign compliance across all aisles.
11. Following PR-14 Emergency evacuation, evacuation routes, alarm sounders, emergency lighting and assembly-point equipment are checked for availability and any obstruction is cleared immediately.
12. For traceability, every intervention is entered in the repair log on the same shift, stating asset identity, fault, parts used, test result and return-to-service time for audit by supervision.

title: Common Rules and Training
text:
1. Report through the on-duty chain on every shift: each employee reports to the shift supervisor running the shift, and the shift supervisor reports to the warehouse manager.
2. Under this structure the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, while the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
3. Work the published roster pattern covering the 6,000 m2 floor: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. Obtain cover for any additional hours in advance, as only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Wear issued personal protective equipment at all times on the warehouse floor: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
6. Keep to segregated routes and clearances: main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide.
7. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse whenever leaving a walkway, making eye contact with drivers before crossing and using only marked pedestrian zones and crossings.
8. Within PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, respect all posted limits: forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.
9. Reduce speed further at interfaces: forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
10. Fasten restraint systems without exception: forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and no new driver may operate until only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators has been satisfied.
11. Complete mandatory training before unsupervised work: PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, and PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
12. Maintain competence in support and safety procedures: PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation, and PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
13. Protect temperature-sensitive stock to specification: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +6 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.
14. Respect hazardous-storage discipline: no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, with access limited to trained and authorised personnel.
15. Attend the evacuation drill that runs every quarter, follow the marshalled route to the assembly point, and remain there because roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.

title: Receiving Slots and Intake
text: 1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. undertakes to receive inbound goods in Zone A, which is the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection served by inbound docks 1-4. 2.
