The building provides 8 dock doors in total, of which dock doors 1-4 are dedicated to inbound receiving and will not be used for routine outbound dispatch. 3. Booking of inbound slots is a firm commitment. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and arrival without an allocated slot will be queued behind booked traffic. 4. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and for inbound they remain the single point of contact for slot allocation, door changes and arrival sequencing. 5. All inbound handling under this Section is executed under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Release to stock is executed under PR-02 Put-away to storage, and no other process will be substituted. 6. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Each inbound delivery is attended by inbound operators from door opening through inspection to system booking. 7. Document check happens before unloading. The inbound team will verify the delivery documentation against the booking before any pallet is removed from the vehicle. 8. Variances in quantity, visible damage or missing documents stop the intake sequence at the door, and the vehicle is held in position until the discrepancy is recorded and disposition is agreed through the defined escalation route. 9. Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system. Counting, condition inspection and label verification are completed in Zone A, and only conforming quantities proceed to system receipt. 10. Goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage. Harborwick commits that no pallet leaves Zone A for storage without a completed system booking under PR-01 Inbound receiving. 11. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller, and inbound doors are maintained ready for scheduled arrivals throughout staffed receiving hours. 12. Receiving operations are resourced with handheld WMS scanning. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, and inbound inspection and booking tasks are prioritised within that pool during intake peaks. 13. Staffed receiving hours are committed as Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Carriers booked inside those windows will be met by inbound operators and allocated a prepared door. 14. Outside those hours intake is only by prior written agreement, and any agreed extension retains the same sequence of document check, then unloading, then inspection, then system booking, then put-away. 15. Harborwick reports intake completion per delivery by booked quantity, received quantity, damage count and system-booking timestamp, providing same-shift visibility that goods are available for put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage.

title: Dispatch Capacity and Release
text:
1. Harborwick provides outbound staging in Zone D in front of docks 5-8 for all scheduled dispatches. Operationally staging capacity is managed to keep staged pallets clear of dock approaches and available for prompt loading. Reliably staged loads are released in door call order to avoid congestion.

2. Altogether the building operates 8 dock doors with maintained access for concurrent inbound and outbound work. Specifically dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch and are reserved for loading and departure activities. Four outbound dock doors remain dedicated to outbound schedules during staffed shifts.

3. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads under client bookings. Carriers receive assigned doors and time slots from the dispatcher before arrival. Timely communication of slot changes keeps waiting time to a minimum.

4. Monday to Friday Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00 for dispatch operations, wrapping and loading. Following that Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, continuing outbound release without interruption. Throughout both shifts dispatcher cover remains available for door allocation and load release.

5. Per shift each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads as committed throughput. Consistently loading performance is sequenced to meet carrier windows within each shift. Beyond scheduled loads, additional movements depend on available door capacity.

6. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg for outbound consignments. Aboard each trailer there are 33 floor pallet positions for floor-loaded pallets. Safely loaded quantity respects both payload and floor-position limits on every departure.

7. Given a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets. Therefore outbound capacity reaches at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift across doors, loads and trailer limits. Fully laden shipments approaching these limits are planned across multiple trailers.

8. Complementing trailers, our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg for smaller consignments. Inside the van there are 6 pallet positions for light orders. Consequently the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

9. Before release toward dispatch, PR-05 Packing and labelling applies to every order container. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing to confirm accuracy before cartons are closed. Afterwards PR-06 Outbound dispatch governs wrapping and load release and loading for all staged orders.

10. Using 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, dispatch wraps every outbound pallet to stable transport condition. Moreover each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller supporting safe bridging between dock and trailer. Ultimately no load is released unless wrapping, documentation and dispatcher release are complete.

title: Operating Hours and Cut-offs
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates the warehouse on two staffed shifts, Monday to Friday.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and provides full receiving, storage, picking and dispatch coverage.
3. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and provides continued receiving, picking, packing and dispatch coverage.
4. Outside these staffed hours no inbound or outbound handling is committed unless additional working has been expressly agreed.
5. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime, and any agreed extension will be confirmed with its supervised hours.
6. The building has 8 dock doors available for scheduled carrier movements within the operating shifts.
7. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
8. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
9. There are 4 outbound dock doors, and outbound capacity is planned exclusively against those doors.
10. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for both inbound and outbound movements.
11. Carriers must arrive within the assigned slot, as late arrival may require rescheduling to the next available door and slot.
12. For inbound receiving, the agreed intake cut-off means booked arrivals received before the cut-off enter same-shift inspection and system booking.
13. Booked arrivals received after the applicable intake cut-off will be received and processed on the next staffed shift.
14. Unbooked or early arrivals will be accommodated only where a door and handling resource remain available without displacing booked slots.
15. For outbound dispatch, the agreed order cut-off means orders released before the cut-off enter same-shift wrapping, staging and loading.
16. Orders released after the applicable dispatch cut-off roll to the next staffed dispatch wave.
17. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift, which sets the disciplined turnaround available to carriers.
18. Consequently, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.
19. Harborwick commits to make that per-shift capacity available when orders and transport have met the agreed cut-offs.
20. Where client volumes exceed the per-shift limit, the excess will be scheduled across following shifts or agreed overtime.
21. Agreed cut-off times apply per shift and per flow, so inbound and outbound cut-offs operate independently.
22. Changes to recurring cut-off times will be agreed in writing and applied from the next operational week unless otherwise confirmed.
23. Daily variations caused by door maintenance, labour constraints or carrier delays will be communicated promptly with a revised door and slot plan.
24. Performance against operating hours, slot adherence and cut-off application will be reported per shift in line with Chapter 1 service levels.

title: Picking and Packing Accuracy
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. maintains Zone C as the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, operated exclusively through scanner-directed tasks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no order is picked from paper lists or memory.

2. Pick-face availability is guaranteed under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Harborwick commits that pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, so each shift begins with saleable stock presented at the face. Bulk reserve remains behind the flow lanes until transferred by replenishment.

3. Order execution is guaranteed under PR-04 Order picking. Every pick is directed by the warehouse management system to a specific location in Zone C. The client receives scan-verified picks where quantity, SKU and location are confirmed in the system at the face.

4. Picking accuracy is supported by a shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners for pickers and inbound staff. Harborwick commits to provide charged, functional scanners for every active picking assignment and to withdraw any faulty unit from use until checked.

5. Harborwick commits that picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. No container passes to packing benches without completed system verification of its contents against the order.

6. Packing and labelling performance is guaranteed under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Harborwick commits to pack, seal, label and check every order container before release toward dispatch. Each parcel and pallet load leaves packing with correct customer labels, shipping marks and documentation inserts.

7. Outbound pallets built from picked orders comply with a maximum gross weight of 900 kg per pallet, including its load. Harborwick commits to weigh-check pallet builds during packing and to split or reconfigure any build that would exceed 900 kg before staging.

8. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers to stabilise palletised orders after packing. Harborwick commits to wrap every outbound pallet to base-to-top stability before transfer from packing toward staging.

9. Harborwick maintains Zone D as the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Packed, labelled and wrapped orders are staged in Zone D by outbound load and door call, protected from damage and ready for collection.

10. For the duration of this agreement Harborwick commits to operate replenishment, picking and packing as one controlled chain. Replenishment under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces enables picking under PR-04 Order picking, verified picking enables work under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and only packed, labelled and weight-compliant pallets enter Zone D for dispatch.

title: Put-away and Storage Accuracy
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. commits to accurate put-away of all booked inventory under PR-02 Put-away to storage.
2. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A before any storage movement begins.
3. Within receiving, inspection of inbound goods is completed before booking into the system.
4. Following system booking, goods are released for put-away to storage without interim diversion.
5. Through this sequence the client receives full system traceability from dock receipt to final storage location.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
7. Across that zone the high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions dedicated to client stock.
8. Against every position Harborwick records pallet identity, SKU, quantity and bay location at the time of put-away.
9. Accordingly the client inventory remains system-directed, with no unbooked pallets held in bulk storage.

10. For weight control a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
11. Beyond pallet level each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
12. Inside bulk storage consignments exceeding bay capacity are split before put-away to protect rack integrity.
13. Consequently storage accuracy includes continuous compliance with both pallet and bay weight limits.

14. Where free block stacking applies, stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height.
15. Separately free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
16. Both height and quantity limits are applied together during put-away planning and floor verification.
17. Toward accuracy assurance, any stack found outside either limit is corrected and rebooked before acceptance as stored.

18. Ultimately Harborwick warrants that booked goods are put away to the assigned Zone B location, within stated rack and stacking limits, with system accuracy maintained from booking through storage.

title: Cycle Counts, Stocktake and Reporting
text:
Harborwick 3PL Ltd guarantees verifiable inventory accuracy through disciplined counting, controlled adjustments and transparent reporting. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, daily assurance and annual verification combine to protect client stock positions without interrupting agreed service continuity.

1. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Assigned ownership ensures every location remains under active control and every variance receives structured investigation. Controllers plan daily tasks, allocate counters, review findings and maintain complete audit records for client stock.

2. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Systematic rotation delivers continuous coverage across storage areas while order fulfilment proceeds normally. Schedules balance workload, prioritise high-movement locations and ensure repeated verification throughout the operating year.

3. Counters record physical quantities independently before any system comparison. Objective methodology requires stock to be counted directly from shelves, pallets and pick faces, with system figures consulted only after the physical result stands recorded. Discrepancies trigger documented follow-up rather than immediate correction.

4. Where an initial count differs from the recorded balance, a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted. Recount discipline prevents transcription errors, misreads or misplaced units from becoming permanent adjustments. Findings from the second check determine whether correction proceeds or deeper investigation continues under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

5. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year. Comprehensive verification covers all client holdings in a single controlled event with frozen movements, assigned count teams and independent checks. Preparation includes advance communication to clients concerning scope, timetable and any temporary constraints on inbound or outbound activity.

6. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Exclusive authority ensures year-end figures receive senior scrutiny before release. Sign-off confirms completeness of counting, review of outstanding variances and approval to post authorised adjustments to the warehouse management system.

7. Accountability for final inventory integrity rests at senior level, because the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Centralised responsibility links counting performance with operational control, safety compliance and client reporting obligations across Harborwick 3PL Ltd.

8. Following each cycle and the annual event, clients receive clear statements of counts completed, variances found, recount outcomes and adjustments posted. Documentation references locations, products, quantities and approvers, enabling reconciliation with client systems. Persistent discrepancies receive root-cause analysis with agreed preventive actions tracked to closure.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will manage all damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, with no damaged stock left in storage, picking or dispatch areas.
2. Any unit found damaged during receiving, storage, picking, packing or dispatch will be segregated immediately and transferred to quarantine without delay for assessment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
3. The quarantine area is in Zone F, within the value-added services area, and only authorized assessment of damaged goods will take place there.
4. Zone F holds the value-added services area, and quarantine holdings there will remain physically separated from saleable, rework and outbound stock at all times.
5. Each quarantine receipt will be identified by product, quantity, location of discovery, nature of damage and date, and system status will be updated to prevent further allocation or dispatch.
6. Photographic evidence and a valuation at cost price in EUR will be completed for every damaged-goods case before any disposal or adjustment proposal is submitted for approval.
7. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and will direct immediate segregation, quarantine transfer and reporting of damaged goods on the shift.
8. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR, and such decisions will be documented with quantity, value and disposition before system posting.
9. Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and no adjustment above that threshold will be posted without that approval.
10. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and retains final authority for damage policy, large write-offs and client reporting.
11. Where damage arises from an operational incident, an incident report will be completed and linked to the quarantine record for traceability.
12. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report, and will confirm corrective action for handling, storage or equipment causes identified through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
13. Clients will receive prompt notification of damage affecting their stock, including quantity, assessed cause, photographs where available, and the approved disposition of restock, rework or scrap.
14. No damaged goods will be returned to saleable stock, reworked or scrapped without documented approval, and all write-off approvals will be retained for audit with the quarantine records.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Returns Inspection and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 days of delivery under PR-07 Returns handling.
2. Eligibility is measured from the recorded delivery date to receipt of the return request, and late requests outside that window will not be accepted as standard returns.
3. All returns are channelled into Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, to keep inspection away from receiving, storage and dispatch flows.
4. Dedicated inspection of every return takes place in Zone F, ensuring consistent handling, segregation and documentation.
5. Trained returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each line.
6. Inspection always occurs BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision, and no unit is returned to stock or directed to rework or scrap without a recorded inspection outcome.
7. Final disposition of each inspected return is approved by the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
8. Accountability for prompt decisions therefore rests with floor leadership on every shift, not with individual handlers.
9. Administrators log receipt, inspection findings and the proposed disposition in the warehouse system on the day of inspection.
10. Clients receive confirmation of acceptance, the inspection result and the approved disposition of restock, rework or scrap.
11. Photographic evidence supports any case involving damage, shortage or suspected misuse, providing a clear audit trail for claims.
12. System inventory is updated only after disposition approval, preserving accuracy between physical holdings and booked stock.
13. Restockable units are returned to saleable inventory in their approved locations once inspection and approval are complete.
14. Reworkable units are transferred to the rework flow with documented instructions, retaining full traceability until re-inspection.
15. Scrapped units are quarantined from saleable stock pending valuation and write-off controls.
16. Timely processing is a contractual commitment: returns received within the 14-day window are inspected promptly and not left unexamined across shifts.
17. Communication on delays, missing documentation or quantity variances is issued to the client without waiting for disposition.
18. Exceptionally, where a return reveals a safety concern, product tampering or repeated defect pattern, an incident report is raised in addition to the PR-07 Returns handling record.
19. Should such an incident report be raised, the shift supervisor reviews every incident report and determines containment, escalation and client notification.
20. Because Zone F concentrates value-added activity, inspection benches, segregation areas and system access remain available for returns on each staffed shift.
21. Consistent application of inspection-then-decision protects clients from premature restocking of defective goods and from unnecessary scrapping of recoverable units.
22. Throughout the process Harborwick retains custody, identification and segregation of client goods until the approved disposition is executed.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides chilled storage in Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C for client stock requiring continuous temperature control.
2. Within Zone E the Client may rely on maintenance of the full compliant band at all times, with lower protection at or above +2 °C and upper protection at or below +6 °C without interruption.
3. All chilled operations are executed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, which governs receipt, storage, monitoring and escalation for every pallet held in the cold zone.
4. Upon arrival chilled inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system, and temperature condition, packaging integrity and documentation form part of that inspection.
5. Following acceptance, goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage, ensuring system traceability precedes any physical transfer to Zone E.
6. Put-away into chilled locations is performed under PR-02 Put-away to storage in coordination with PR-12 Cold-chain handling, preserving cold-chain continuity during transfer.
7. During every shift Harborwick manually verifies cold-zone temperature each shift and records the verified reading for audit and client reporting.
8. Continuous monitoring supplements the manual verification, and any excursion below +2 °C or above +6 °C triggers immediate containment, notification and documented corrective action under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
9. Affected chilled pallets remain isolated in Zone E pending assessment, and no compromised stock is released for order fulfilment without agreed disposition.
10. For transparency the Client receives shift verification records and excursion reports on request, with storage temperature history traceable by location and time period.
11. Harborwick commits to maintain Zone E capacity, calibrated monitoring equipment and trained personnel sufficient to sustain the +2 to +6 °C commitment across all contracted chilled volumes.
